source.title: A Progressive Batching L-BFGS Method for Machine Learning
source.authors: Raghu Bollapragada; Dheevatsa Mudigere; J. Nocedal; H. Shi; P. Tang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The authors report their own neural-network results comparing progressive batching with fixed-batch methods and describe late full-batch overfitting, refining the claim about when batch size affects generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracies for progressive-batching L-BFGS, SG, and Adam, but does not isolate batch size: the methods also differ in optimizer and training schedule. Its discussion of prior large-batch studies is not treated as a result.
record.test_reason: The SG and Adam baselines directly compare held-out image-classification accuracy under limited tuning, bearing on V4. The proposed PBQN comparisons do not test V5: batch size, optimizer and schedule change together, without a fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report broadly similar test accuracy for PBQN, greater gradient-evaluation requirements, and late full-batch overfitting. Their conclusions are preliminary; competitive parallel training remains prospective and requires algorithmic improvements.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes progressive-batching L-BFGS and compares it with fixed-batch SG and Adam; it does not reproduce a controlled large-batch versus small-batch experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that results depend on the curvature-vector variant (multi-batch versus full overlap) and lightly tunes PBQN's θ; the best θ differs across the displayed neural-network plots.

fits_no_version.finding: Progressive-batching L-BFGS attains broadly similar best test accuracies to SG and Adam, with more gradient evaluations and fewer iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Progressive-batching quasi-Newton training can attain competitive held-out accuracy, with computational tradeoffs.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report worsening test loss and accuracy after substantial additional full-batch PBQN training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prolonged full-batch PBQN training can overfit; this does not isolate a fixed-epoch large-batch penalty.

record.problems: The neural-network study is described as preliminary. Batch size is confounded with optimizer and training schedule, comparisons are not controlled at fixed epochs, and Table 1 reports best test accuracy over 5 runs without uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed to fit the training set.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, adaptive optimizers other than Adam, momentum SGD, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay and switching optimizers. Table 1 does not establish matched training performance at the selected test-accuracy checkpoints.
The fixed-epoch large-batch penalty and its removal through longer training, warmup, learning-rate scaling or normalization and regularization changes.
Dropout effects; dropout is omitted from every tested neural-network method.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and comparing with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 values are transcribed correctly and are percentages. They are best test accuracies over five runs and initializations, not means or matched-budget endpoints. The reversed V4 row states describe numerical direction only. Because V4 says adaptive methods often perform worse, these modest counterexamples qualify its scope rather than overturning it.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons as a test of optimizer generalization under matched tuning.
No fixed-epoch controlled batch-size comparison; no systematic large-batch sweep, warmup, or normalization and regularization changes.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the train-test gap.

relationships.condition: SG versus Adam on four MNIST/CIFAR-10 convolutional networks, batch size 128, development-based learning-rate decay, without batch normalization or dropout
relationships.reason: Adam's best test accuracy exceeds SG's on every network by 0.09–0.79 percentage points (R1–R2, R5–R6, R9–R10, R13–R14), identifying settings without the proposed adaptive-optimizer disadvantage; best-of-five reporting provides no uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Reported best-test-accuracy advantages of 0.09–0.79 percentage points remain unverified, with best-of-five reporting lacking uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 and MNIST networks; progressive-batching L-BFGS compared with fixed-batch SG and Adam
